xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2351: Overdeck Anywhere P0: scoped access tokens + WS/SSE heartbeats (security prerequisites)

plan.title: Overdeck Anywhere P0: scoped access tokens + WS/SSE heartbeats (security prerequisites)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: PAN-4435 (sibling: Settings token UI + require_token_mint toggle)

metadata.sizeJustification: One security boundary that must land together: once a kind 'token' record can be created (W7 routes, W8 CLI), every call site that assumes 'registry credential = admin device' or 'any credential = root' becomes an escalation path (root-session mint, pairing issuance, device revocation, both gates). The scope model, credential resolution, both gate checks and the mint/pairing hardening therefore ship in one PR. The surface is 34 files, but 15 are tests or test fixtures beside the code they cover and 4 are docs; the subsystem count is inflated because the lint counts each doc file as its own subsystem. The separable parts were already split out: /ws/terminal heartbeat to PAN-4434 and the Settings UI + require_token_mint toggle to PAN-4435.

narratives.Problem: Every registry credential is an admin device today: AccessTokenScope is only 'admin' and both the remote request gate and the WebSocket upgrade gate pass any credential. Remote consumers in epic PAN-2350 (phone, Hermes, SSE sidecars) would all hold root, so a leaked sidecar credential equals a leaked machine. Adding a narrower token also exposes four call sites (session mint, pairing issuance, device revocation, the two gates) that would let a token escalate to root.
narratives.Proposal: Extend the PAN-3762 registry (src/lib/access-tokens.ts) with six scopes and scopeSatisfies; resolve Bearer-only kind 'token' credentials carrying scopes; enforce one route-scope table (route-scopes.ts, default admin) in the remote request gate and authorizeDashboardUpgrade (/ws/terminal needs operate); refuse session mint, pairing issuance and device revocation to tokens; let Bearer odk_ requests skip CSRF and the missing-Origin rule; add GET/POST/DELETE /api/access-tokens and pan token create|list|revoke; prove the read:events acceptance line end to end; document it. The /ws/terminal heartbeat moved to PAN-4434 and the Settings UI/toggle to PAN-4435; /ws/rpc and /events/stream already send 15 s heartbeats.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No /ws/terminal heartbeat or XTerminal.tsx change (PAN-4434).
- No Settings UI section and no config-yaml schema entry or Settings toggle for require_token_mint (PAN-4435).
- No ?token= query-parameter authentication on WebSocket upgrades or HTTP routes.
- No session cookie minted for any token credential, and no browser session for non-admin identities.
- No token expiry, rotation or per-token rate limits.
- No removal or change of OVERDECK_EVENTS_TOKEN, the internal token, the root session cookie, or device pairing behavior for devices.
- No route-scope table rows beyond the PRD table; everything else stays admin.
- No change to loopback peer trust for requests that present no credential.
- No raise of any cap in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt.
- No new heartbeat on /ws/rpc or /events/stream (both already send 15 s heartbeats).
- No change to GET /a/:slug host-gated public artifact serving.

autoDecisions.summary: Split the /ws/terminal heartbeat into PAN-4434 and the Settings token UI plus require_token_mint schema entry/toggle into PAN-4435; PAN-2351 keeps the scope model, enforcement, routes, CLI and docs.
autoDecisions.rationale: The combined plan exceeded the finalize plan-size lint, and both split parts ship and verify independently (heartbeat needs its own idle-proxy check; the UI needs Playwright UAT). The remaining core is one security boundary.

autoDecisions.summary: Enforce scopes at the two gates (remote request gate, authorizeDashboardUpgrade) from one route-scope table with default admin, instead of an optional requiredScope parameter on every route helper.
autoDecisions.rationale: The global gate already sees every /api and /events request and the upgrade gate every /ws socket, so one table cannot drift between call sites, and unlisted routes fail closed.

autoDecisions.summary: Tokens authenticate only via Authorization: Bearer; drop the planned ?token= query parameter.
autoDecisions.rationale: Query tokens leak into proxy and access logs; programmatic WebSocket clients can set headers; header-only tokens make the CSRF/Origin relaxation safe.

autoDecisions.summary: Only root credentials may create access tokens, issue pairing credentials or revoke other devices; a token never mints a session.
autoDecisions.rationale: Extends PAN-3762's rule that a device cannot mint devices and prevents a revocable credential from turning into the unrevocable root session.

autoDecisions.summary: Start the route-scope table minimal: read:events on the event stream, five non-secret state reads, four conversation reads, three message routes for tell, /ws/terminal for operate.
autoDecisions.rationale: Default-deny is the safe posture; each future consumer widens the table in its own issue with review.

autoDecisions.summary: pan token revoke goes through DELETE /api/access-tokens/:id and falls back to a direct registry write only when the dashboard is unreachable; create and list use the registry directly.
autoDecisions.rationale: Copies the pan devices revoke precedent, closes live connections at once, and needs no new cross-process notification machinery.

autoDecisions.summary: Treat a registry record with no kind as a device and carry scopes on device credentials too.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-3762 always writes kind 'device'; honoring the stored scopes means a hand-edited narrow record is never silently widened.

autoDecisions.summary: The per-route helpers rejectUnauthorizedDashboardRequest/rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest read the same route-scope table; DELETE /api/access-tokens/:id is root-only (no token self-revoke).
autoDecisions.rationale: GET /knowledge-viewer/* sits outside the gate's /api and /events prefixes and relies on the helper, so the helper must enforce scope too; reading the same table keeps one source of truth, and root-only revocation keeps the token surface consistent with D-11.

items.title: Add the six-scope model and scopeSatisfies to the access-token registry

expected_outputs: tests/unit/lib/access-tokens.test.ts passes including the scopeSatisfies matrix

narrative.Action: PRD W1. In src/lib/access-tokens.ts replace `export type AccessTokenScope = 'admin';` (:35) with the exported ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPES tuple ['read:events','read:state','read:conversations','tell','operate','admin'] and the derived union type. Add exported scopeSatisfies(granted: readonly string[], required): true when granted includes 'admin' or required, or required === 'tell' and granted includes 'operate'. Add exported parseAccessTokenScopes(input: string | readonly string[]) that splits a comma list, trims, deduplicates, throws an Error naming the first unknown scope, and throws on an empty set. createAccessToken (:206-224) validates: name trimmed non-empty and <= 200 chars; scopes pass parseAccessTokenScopes; errors name the bad field. Keep isRecord accepting any string scopes (unknown scopes simply satisfy nothing). Update the module header to describe scopes and kinds. Add the named tests from PRD W1 to tests/unit/lib/access-tokens.test.ts.

Enforce the route-scope table in the remote request gate and route auth helpers

metadata.acJustification: Six criteria because this item owns both HTTP enforcement points (the global gate and the per-route helpers) that share one table; splitting them would let one land without the other.
metadata.readinessReason: Runs in its own slot after credential-scopes; its new files (route-scopes.ts, route-scopes.test.ts) are unique to it, and its dashboard-auth.ts edit is ordered after credential-scopes by a blocks edge.

narrative.Action: PRD W3. Create src/dashboard/server/route-scopes.ts importing only from ../../lib/access-tokens.js. Move the pure gatePathname function (remote-request-gate.ts:54-76) into it unchanged and re-export it from remote-request-gate.ts (`export { gatePathname } from './route-scopes.js';`). In route-scopes.ts export ROUTE_SCOPES with exactly the HTTP rows of the PRD route-scope table, WS_TERMINAL_SCOPE = 'operate', and requiredScopeFor(method, pathname) that matches exact case-sensitive paths where a ':param' segment matches one non-empty segment, returning 'admin' when nothing matches. In remote-request-gate.ts change remoteGateRejection (:99-109) to return { status: 401 } | { status: 403; missingScope } | null: when resolveDashboardCredential returns a credential, return null only if scopeSatisfies(credentialScopes(credential), requiredScopeFor(request.method, pathname)), else { status: 403, missingScope } — never fall back to loopback trust for a credentialed request. The middleware (:115) answers 403 with { error: 'insufficient_scope', missingScope } and keeps 401 { error: 'unauthorized' }. Update the module header rule list. Add the named PRD W3 tests; route-scopes.test.ts imports NO_LOSS_MATRIX and never reads source files. Defense in depth (D-6): in routes/dashboard-auth.ts rejectUnauthorizedDashboardRequest (:353-364), after the 401 check, compute the required scope with requiredScopeFor(request.method, gatePathname(request.url)) (a null pathname means 'admin') and return 403 { error: 'insufficient_scope', missingScope } when the credential's scopes do not satisfy it; rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest inherits this. This covers GET /knowledge-viewer/* (routes/knowledge-viewer.ts:272-277), which is outside the gate's prefixes. GET /a/:slug (host-gated public artifacts) is unchanged.

narrative.Action: PRD W9. New test composing Layer.mergeAll(remoteRequestGateLayer, eventsRouteLayer, a stub POST /api/agents/:id/tell route, accessTokensRouteLayer) with the harness style of remote-request-gate.test.ts, plus a direct authorizeDashboardUpgrade call with WS_TERMINAL_SCOPE. Case 1 (LAN peer, read:events token): SSE 200 text/event-stream; tell 403 insufficient_scope/missingScope 'tell'; terminal upgrade 403; then DELETE /api/access-tokens/:id with the internal token ends the open SSE stream and a new GET /events/stream returns 401. Case 2: write revokedAt straight into access-tokens.json (simulating pan token revoke with no dashboard), run startAccessTokenRefresh() under vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setInterval','clearInterval','Date'] }), advance 5000 ms, flush, and assert the next GET /events/stream returns 401. No real setTimeout waits. Implementation checkpoint: no existing test mounts eventsRouteLayer (it calls getEventStore() and retainAllAgentOutputInterest()). Try the real layer with a temporary OVERDECK_HOME first; if the event store cannot initialize in a unit test, fall back to a stub GET /events/stream that returns a text/event-stream body wrapped in endStreamOnDeviceRevocation(stream, resolveDashboardCredential(headers)) behind the real gate, and say so in the test header comment.
